title: Starship equipment
description: A part a ship is fitted with: a weapon, its ammunition, armour, shields, a reactor, a power coupling or a hyperdrive. Every starship carries one of each system without spending a modification slot, which is what separates this type from starship-modification — equipment is what the hull comes with and can be swapped, a modification is what is bolted on afterwards and costs slots. The fields a shipyard list needs (category, cost) are always present; each category then carries its own block, because nothing a hyperdrive records is meaningful for a shield.

key.description: Stable slug identifying this part. Derived from the name once and never reused, so a saved loadout keeps resolving after a rename.

name.description: Display name, in sentence case as printed on the shipyard tables.

sourceKey.description: Key of the source this part was published in, matching a document of the source content type.

contentSet.description: Whether this belongs to the core rules or to the community expanded-content supplement.

category.description: What kind of part this is. It decides which of the optional blocks below apply and which table the part is printed in: only a weapon carries the weapon block, only ammunition carries firedBy, and the four system categories each carry exactly one block of their own.

costInCredits.description: List price in credits for a Small ship. Prices for every other hull are this figure scaled by the Starship Size Equipment Cost table, so the raw number is stored rather than a per-size table. Zero on the slower hyperdrives, which are the ones a hull is assumed to already have.

description.description: Markdown explaining what the part does beyond its table row. Present on the systems, whose behaviour cannot be read off a row, and absent on most weapons, whose row says everything.

weapon.description: Where the weapon is fitted and what scale of hull it belongs to. Present on weapons only.

mounting.description: Which of the four weapon mountings the part occupies. The mounting decides who fires it and how: primary weapons are aimed by the helm, secondary by a gunner, tertiary launchers throw the ammunition of this same content type, and quaternary weapons drop mines and bombs behind the ship.

weaponSize.description: Which of the two weapon tables the part is printed in: small covers Tiny to Large hulls, huge covers Huge and Gargantuan. The same weapon usually appears in both at a different damage die, as two separate parts, which is why this is a property of the part rather than of the ship.

properties.description: Weapon properties as printed on the table row, one clause per entry, each carrying its own numeric argument: "burst 6", "overheat 2", "constitution 15". The leading word of every clause names a property defined in the Weapon Properties section of the starship rules. The range clause is not among them, because range is a field of its own.

damage.description: Damage on a hit, before ability modifiers and properties. Absent on the tertiary and quaternary launchers, which deal no damage themselves — the ammunition they fire does.

damageForLargerShips.description: The bracketed damage printed beside the first, which applies when the ammunition is fired from a Huge or larger hull. Ammunition only: a weapon states its two scales as two separate parts instead.

weightInPounds.description: Weight of one piece of ammunition, which counts against the ship's cargo capacity. Ammunition only; the systems are part of the hull and are never weighed.

weightInPoundsForLargerShips.description: The bracketed weight printed beside the first, for ammunition fired from a Huge or larger hull.

range.description: The two range bands in feet. Attacks beyond normal range and within long range are made at disadvantage, and nothing can be attacked beyond long range.

firedBy.description: Names of the launchers this ammunition fits, each matching a starship-equipment document of category weapon. Ammunition is grouped under its launcher in the printed table and is useless without one, so the link is recorded rather than left for a reader to infer from the name.

armor.description: What the armour does. Present on armour only.

armorClass.description: The ship's armor class formula while wearing this armour, as printed, including the cap it puts on Dexterity: "10 + Dex modifier (max 2)". Stored as text because the cap is part of the value, matching how personal armour is recorded.

damageReduction.description: Damage subtracted from every hit taken from an attack roll. Zero on lightweight armour, which trades reduction for keeping the whole Dexterity modifier.

stealthDisadvantage.description: Whether the armour imposes disadvantage on the ship's attempts to go unnoticed. Always present, including when false, so a sheet can read it without a null check.

shield.description: How the shields trade capacity against recovery. Present on shields only, and the two values always move in opposite directions: fortress shields hold half again as much and recharge two-thirds as fast, quick-charge shields do the reverse.

capacityMultiplier.description: Multiplier applied to the ship's base shield points, as printed: "x 3/2". Text rather than a number because the book states it as a fraction and rounding it to a decimal would change the arithmetic.

regenerationRateCoefficient.description: Multiplier applied to the maximum value of the ship's shield die to give the points recovered each round, as printed.

reactor.description: What the reactor produces and what it costs to run. Present on reactors only.

powerDiceRecovered.description: Power dice recovered at the start of each of the ship's turns, as printed. Text rather than a number because two of the three reactors state it as a roll: a power core recovers 1d2 and an ionization reactor 1d2-1.

fuelCostModifier.description: Multiplier applied to the ship's fuel costs, as printed. Absent on the fuel cell reactor, which is the baseline the other two are stated relative to.

powerCoupling.description: Where the coupling lets power dice be stored. Present on power couplings only, and every coupling sets at least one of the two: a direct coupling stores centrally, a distributed one stores per system, and a hub and spoke coupling does both at a lower capacity.

centralStorageCapacity.description: Power dice held in the ship's central capacitor, available to any system.

systemStorageCapacity.description: Power dice held at each individual system, available only to that system.

hyperdriveClass.description: The drive's class, which multiplies the time a jump takes: a class 0.5 drive is the fastest in the book and a class 15 the slowest. Text rather than a number because the printed classes mix decimals and whole numbers and the leading zero of "0.5" is part of how the class is named.

dieFaces.description: Faces on each die: the 6 of 3d6.

type.description: Damage type, which decides how a target's armour and shields apply. Ion damage is the one that strips shields and disables systems rather than breaching hull. Absent on the few pieces of ammunition whose whole effect is a special rule rather than damage.
